headline: Leaning higher, but expect big swings
text: US futures are up ahead of the open (S&P +1.72%, Nasdaq +2.45%), with Europe higher and Asia mostly up.
Helping: Europe, Asia, Copper, Stocks above 200-day. Weighing: 10-year yield, Gold, S&P 500 vs 200-day, VIX.

Expect a jumpy session: the VIX is high at 25.2, SPY options gamma is negative (dealers' hedging makes moves bigger). Gaps and reversals are common in these conditions, so a small early move says little.
Options price a typical day of about ±1.9% for the S&P 500 (about 7,170–7,443); historically about 82% of days stay inside that.
On past days with VIX between 25 and 30 and the VIX curve normal (since 1990, 318 days), the next session closed higher 54% of the time (all days: 54%), with a typical move of 0.9% (all days: 0.5%).

drivers.name: US futures
drivers.note: S&P +1.72% · Nasdaq +2.45% vs the last close. The clearest hint of how the day opens.

drivers.name: Dollar index
drivers.note: A sharply stronger dollar usually weighs on US stocks (tighter money, weaker overseas earnings).

drivers.name: 10-year yield
drivers.note: At 4.90%. Fast-rising yields hurt growth and tech stocks; falling yields help them.

drivers.name: WTI oil
drivers.note: $84.57. A big oil jump feeds inflation worries; energy stocks move with it.

drivers.name: Gold
drivers.note: $3670. A strong gold bid often means investors are looking for safety.

drivers.name: Copper
drivers.note: “Dr. Copper”: rising copper = traders expect more growth.

drivers.name: Bitcoin
drivers.note: Trades all weekend and night: a read on risk appetite while Wall Street is shut.

drivers.name: S&P 500 vs 200-day
drivers.note: Below the 200-day = long-term downtrend: rallies have tended to get sold.

drivers.name: Stocks above 200-day
drivers.note: How many big US stocks are in their own uptrend.

drivers.name: VIX
drivers.note: Below 16 calm, above 25 nervous, above 30 fear.

drivers.name: VIX curve
drivers.note: Normal (below 1): no panic in the options market.

drivers.name: Market mood
drivers.note: Neutral: the site's 0–100 fear/greed gauge from 10 readings. Extremes often mark turning points, so it sets the tone rather than the direction.

levels.name: SPY gamma flip
levels.note: Above it dealers calm moves down; below it they speed them up.

levels.name: SPY call wall
levels.note: Biggest call position: often acts as a ceiling.

levels.name: SPY put wall
levels.note: Biggest put position: often acts as a floor; a break can speed up selling.

levels.name: SPY put wall by today's volume
levels.note: Where today's new put trading is concentrated: shows the floor shifting during the session.

base.label: VIX between 25 and 30 and the VIX curve normal

scenarios.text: Above 730 (put wall) is where rallies often stall.
Yesterday's S&P 500 range was 6,970–7,199: a break of either end is the first real sign of direction.

tips: Size smaller than usual and use the “wrong if” level on every alert.
